title.rendered: Driving Accountability through Dialogue –  Interface and Feedback Session in Monze District

content.rendered:
Following a successful issue identification process, communities from Manungu, Makonka, and Mulongalwili came together for an Interface Meeting and Feedback Session supported by WaterAid Zambia under the Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Revolution (WASH-R) Project.

The engagement provided a platform for open dialogue between community representatives and key stakeholders, including the Council Chairperson, Director Health Services (represented), SWASCO (represented), the Manungu Ward Councilor, and Ward Development Committees (WDCs).

In his opening remarks, the Council Chairperson thanked WaterAid Zambia for its continued support to the district, highlighting that the ongoing WASH interventions in healthcare facilities and schools are a testament to a better Monze a model for other districts.

He further encouraged communities to regularly convene and speak out when things are not going well, emphasizing that accountability begins with collective engagement.

During the session, community members directly interacted with their leaders — asking questions, sharing feedback, and presenting challenges related to water, sanitation, hygiene, and other pressing development issues.

The Interface and Feedback Session served as a vital step in strengthening trust, transparency, and responsiveness between duty bearers and the people they serve.

title.rendered: Monze District Records Steady Progress on Road Works Under Presidential Directive

content.rendered:
Monze District has recorded significant progress in road infrastructure development across its three constituencies—Monze Central, Moomba, and Bweengwa—under the Presidential Directive funded through the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) allocation of K3,278,013.69.

Speaking in an interview, Monze Town Council Public Relations Officer Kanchele Kanchele said a combined total of 75 Kilometers of road works have been completed out  of a total of 105.4 Kilometers allocated under the Presidential Directive, while works on the remaining 30.4 Kilometers are underway across the District.

Kanchele explained that in Monze Central Constituency a total road chainage of 38 km  was earmarked to be worked on and that 29 km had been completed.

He said the works on the Malama Road which had been allocated 15 km has been completed and that the Chisekesi–St. Mary’s Road 5 km has been cleared and grubbed, adding that the Off St. Mary’s to Gali Road allocated 9 km has been completed with ongoing spot improvements.

Kanchele said In Moomba Constituency a total road chainage of 33.2 km  was the target and  24 km completed with works still ongoing, and  an additional 6.2 km cleared and grubbed.

He explained that notable works included full completion of Hamudonga–Kasaka Road 15 km, and partial works on George Artkins to Kasaka Road and the route to Kanyondwe School.

As for Bweengwa Constituency, Kanchele said a total chainage of 34.2 km was targeted to be worked on but only 22 km has been completed so far and work are ongoing.

The Main highlights include full completion of Keemba–Kaumuzya Road (15 km), with ongoing works on Niko–Bbolomani Road and pending commencement on Niko–Malundu Road.

Kanchele said the Local Authority remains committed to completing all the remaining roads works before the end of the year which is inclusive of the feeder roads as some strecthes have commenced dumping activities.

title.rendered: Bridging the Gap: How Three Constituency Ambulances Will Transform Health Service Delivery in Monze District.

content.rendered:
Monday marked a turning point in Monze District’s health narrative as the Monze Town Council officially handed over two ambulances to the Ministry of Health through the Local Authority.

The vehicles, earmarked for Moomba and Bweengwa Constituencies, were procured centrally by the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development using the 2023 Constituency Development Fund (CDF).

Their arrival signals a new era of responsive healthcare—one that promises to save lives, restore dignity, and strengthen rural resilience.

A History of Struggle: The Pain of Delayed Access

For years, rural communities in Monze District have faced the harsh reality of inadequate emergency transport. The district has long depended on a single ambulance to service patients across three constituencies—Monze Central, Moomba, and Bweengwa. This critical shortage meant that patients in life-threatening conditions were often ferried on ox-carts, bicycles, or private vehicles, if available at all.

In remote areas like Moomba and Bweengwa, the journey to the nearest hospital could span over an hour, with poor road networks compounding the delay. Many families mourned loved ones lost not to the severity of illness, but to the cruel passage of time. Health workers, too, bore the brunt—referrals were delayed, outreach programs were limited, and morale suffered. The lack of mobility undermined the very essence of responsive healthcare.

A New Dawn: The Arrival of Constituency Ambulances

The handover ceremony at Monze Civic Centre was more than symbolic—it was a declaration of intent. Moomba Member of Parliament Hon. Fred Chaatila emphasized that the ambulances reflect government’s commitment to ensuring no life is lost due to delayed access to care.

“These vehicles are not just machines. They are lifelines,” Hon. Chaatila said. He further assured that the Moomba CDF Committee is prioritizing road rehabilitation to ensure smooth and swift patient transport.

Bweengwa MP Hon. Michelo Kasauta added a note of caution and civic responsibility, urging the health department to recruit sober-minded drivers.

“Let us treat these vehicles with care, compassion, and vigilance,” he said, stressing that the ambulances are sacred vessels meant to carry the sick—not to be misused or mishandled.

Mobile Bridges of Hope

Monze District Commissioner Mwanza Malambo captured the broader vision, describing the ambulances as mobile bridges between rural clinics and hospitals.

In a district where distances often separate patients from lifesaving interventions, these vehicles will close the gap—literally and figuratively.

From maternal emergencies to accident response, from outreach campaigns to inter-facility referrals, the ambulances will empower health workers and restore public trust in the system.

Grounded in Data: The Referral Burden

Providing context to the handover, Director of Public Health Dr. Gocho Kapoba shared referral statistics that underscore the urgency of the intervention.

“Between Monze Central, Bweengwa, and Moomba Constituencies, the district recorded a total of 129 maternal cases, 17 neonatal cases, and 52 clinical cases requiring ambulance referrals—figures that underscore the urgent need for dedicated emergency transport across all regions.”

“Together, Moomba and Bweengwa Constituencies recorded over 80 ambulance referrals—including 50 maternal,7 neonatal, and 28 clinical cases—all previously dependent on a single district ambulance, underscoring the life-saving significance of the newly allocated vehicles,” He said.

These figures reflect just a portion of the referral burden previously shouldered by a single ambulance. With Monze Central Constituency set to receive its own ambulance in the next batch, the district is steadily moving toward equitable and efficient emergency response.

A Call to Community Stewardship

While the government has delivered the tools, their impact depends on collective stewardship. Community members, health staff, and local leaders must ensure the ambulances are maintained, monitored, and used ethically. Transparency in scheduling, accountability in fuel usage, and respect for patient dignity must guide their operation.

Conclusion:

From Crisis to Capacity

The handover of the three constituency ambulances—two for Moomba and Bweengwa, and one previously allocated—signals a story of transformation: from crisis to capacity, from neglect to empowerment.

As the engines roar to life, may they carry not just patients, but the hopes of a district determined to rise.

title.rendered: From Pit Latrines to Progress: How CDF Is Transforming Communities in Monze

content.rendered:
In the heart of Southern Province, Monze District is quietly rewriting its development story—one ablution block, classroom, and water reticulation system at a time. Thanks to the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), communities that once struggled with basic infrastructure are now experiencing tangible change, dignity, and hope.

Manungu’s Sanitation Breakthrough

For years, Manungu Primary and Secondary School in Monze Central Constituency operated without running water or proper sanitation facilities. Pupils relied on pit latrines—often flooded during the rainy season—and girls routinely missed classes during menstruation due to the lack of privacy and hygiene.

That changed on August 26th, 2025, when Hon. Jack Mwiimbu, Member of Parliament and Minister of Home Affairs and Internal Security, officially handed over a newly constructed ablution block and water reticulation system. Built under the 2024 CDF community project component, the facility has become a beacon of transformation.

“Girls no longer have to miss classes whenever they are attending,” says Lumuno Habanzu, a Form 1 pupil.

“The boys are now eager to participate in sports after class because of the showers,” adds Dalisto Phiri, Grade 11.

Beyond sports, the showers are a lifeline for pupils from water-scarce areas. Many now go home refreshed, no longer burdened by the daily search for bathing water.

Community-Led, Government-Backed

The Manungu project began as a grassroots initiative. When the community faced challenges in mobilizing funds, they turned to the CDF—an empowering move that reflects the fund’s core purpose: enabling citizens to shape their own development.

According to the [2025 CDF sensitization report](https://www.monzecouncil.gov.zm/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/2025-BUDGET-CONSULTATIVE-MEETING-MINUTES.pdf), Monze Central Constituency held consultative meetings across all 12 wards, encouraging residents to apply for community projects. Priorities ranged from sanitation and water systems to classroom blocks, market shelters, and road rehabilitation.

Beyond Manungu: A District on the Move

Monze Town Council has since commenced construction of dozens of CDF-funded projects for 2025 in all the three Constituencies of the District.

Each project is a response to community needs, vetted through feasibility assessments and stakeholder engagement.

A Model for Inclusive Development

The success of CDF in Monze is not just about infrastructure—it’s about restoring dignity, boosting school attendance, and fostering civic pride. It’s about girls like Lumuno and boys like Dalisto who now see school as a place of opportunity, not hardship.

Hon. Mwiimbu’s message during the Manungu handover was clear: development is a shared responsibility. By linking local progress to national stability, he underscored the power of unity and participation.

The Road Ahead

As Monze continues to implement its 2025 CDF projects, the district is fast becoming a model for community-driven development. The challenge now is to sustain momentum, strengthen project management practices and ensure that every kwacha spent delivers lasting impact.

And if Manungu is any indication, the future looks promising—cleaner, safer, and more inclusive.

title.rendered: MONZE TOWN COUNCIL’S OSCAR CHILANGA ADMITTED AS ASSOCIATE MEMBER OF ILGAZ

content.rendered:
Monze Town Council is proud to announce that Mr. Oscar Chilanga, Director of Human Resource and Administration, has been officially admitted as an Associate Member of the Institute of Local Government Administrators of Zambia (ILGAZ).

 

The admission ceremony took place on Friday, 8th August 2025, during a vibrant and well-attended dinner event held in Lusaka.

 

Mr. Chilanga began his distinguished career in local government in 1993 at Siavonga Town Council, where he served as a Works Foreman. Over the past 32 years, he has contributed to the development of seven local authorities across Zambia including Siavonga twice, Kalomo, Kazungula, Mpika, and Monze twice, holding various key positions including:

 

– Community Development Officer 

– Deputy Director of Planning

– Water Coordinator 

– Director of Planning 

– Director of Works 

– Chief Administrative Officer 

 

Currently, Mr. Chilanga serves as both Deputy Council Secretary and Director of Human Resource and Administration at Monze Town Council.

 

His admission into ILGAZ is a testament to his unwavering dedication, vast experience, and continued commitment to excellence in local governance.

title.rendered: FEEDER ROADS IN MONZE SPRING BACK TO LIFE, BOOSTING ACCESS AND AGRICULTURAL FLOW

content.rendered:
Monze District is witnessing a quiet but profound transformation. Following President Hakainde Hichilema’s directive that all local authorities prioritize the rehabilitation of feeder roads, Monze Town Council has responded with purposeful urgency—reopening critical routes that have long endured neglect.

The directive, aligning perfectly with last year’s bumper harvest, is proving to be a timely boost for farmers’ eager to move their grain to strategic depots.

In Moomba Constituency, the Hamudonga Road is breathing new life into Mwanza East’s farming communities.

Earth-moving equipment are seen opening up the road, as farmers load grain destined for the Food Reserve Agency (FRA). This route has become more than just a transport link—it’s a lifeline and will only continue improve accessibility for the locals.

“Hamudonga Road is more than a shortcut; it’s our economic artery,” said Councilor Abel Hachambwa of Mwanza Ward. “With the road open, our farmers can move produce faster and we can receive social services that were once difficult to access.”

Local headman Chibinda of Bwantu echoed this sentiment saying health services, education, and other vital amenities are now within practical reach, thanks to improved connectivity.

In Monze Central Constituency, the Hamapande Road—once a dusty trail deemed impassable—is also undergoing rehabilitation.

Years of community frustration are giving way to a renewed sense of optimism.

“This road was forgotten for far too long,” noted a local resident Prosper Mwiinba of Hamapande. “Now, we’re seeing machinery, progress, and the promise of development.”

And speaking during an on-site interview following the inspection of ongoing works on the Hamudonga Road in Moomba Ward, Monze Town Council Secretary Mr. Beston Kajoba reaffirmed the local authority’s commitment to improving rural connectivity and infrastructure through targeted Constituency Development Fund (CDF) investments.

Mr. Kajoba disclosed that the Council has earmarked three critical road networks for maintenance under the current K3.2 million Presidential Directive CDF allocation.

He said these roads include Hamudongo Road in Moomba Constituency, Hamapande Road in Monze Central Constituency and Kaumuzya–Keemba Road in Bweengwa Constituency.

“These roads were selected based on their strategic importance to local mobility, access to social services, and economic activity. The interventions are not just cosmetic; they are designed to enhance long-term durability and resilience,” stated Mr. Kajoba.

He further explained that the planned scope of works on includes grading to improve surface smoothness and vehicle accessibility, drainage formation which aims to mitigate waterlogging and erosion during rainy seasons, spot improvements targeting critical sections prone to wear and tear a comprehensive rehabilitation to restore structural integrity and ensure sustainability of the roads. 

Mr. Kajoba emphasized that the Council is working closely with local contractors and community stakeholders to ensure transparency, quality assurance, and timely delivery.

He also noted that these road upgrades will significantly reduce travel time, improve access to health and education facilities, and stimulate local economic growth—particularly in agriculture and trade.

“These are not just roads; they are lifelines for our communities,” he said.

As work continues, the roads are not only carving new paths through terrain—but rewriting the local development story, one stretch of gravel at a time

title.rendered: NON FUNCTIONAL TRAFFIC LIGHTS TO BE REPLACED-MTC

content.rendered:
Monze Town Council has officially commenced the process of overhauling the non-functional traffic lights at the intersection of Chivuna/St Mary’s road and Livingston road, marking a significant step toward improving road safety and traffic management in the Central Business District.

 

On Wednesday morning, council officials led a site visit with local contractors to the intersection of Chivuna/St Mary’s Road and Livingstone Road, where the existing signal system has remained inactive for months and the bustling junction of Harry Mwanga Nkumbula Road near Puma Filling Station, which is set to receive a brand-new traffic light installation.

 

PUBLIC RELATIONS OFFICER KANCHELE KANCHELE CONFIRMED THE DEVELOPMENT STATING THAT THE MOVE IS MEANT TO MODERNIZE THE DISTRICT’S CBD.

 

 “This initiative reflects our commitment to modernizing Monze’s urban infrastructure. The selected intersections are critical for managing increasing vehicular movement and ensuring pedestrian safety. We are pleased to see strong interest from local contractors, which aligns with our goal of promoting community participation and transparency in public procurement.”

 

The project, funded by the Ministry of Transport through the Road Transport and Safety Agency (RTSA), includes the complete overhaul of the signal system at the Great North Road (T1 Livingstone Road) and Chivuna Road junction, as well as the installation of a new system at Harry Mwanga Nkumbula Road and Livingstone Road near Puma filling station.

 

Mr. Kanchele added: “We urge residents to support this initiative, which is part of our broader urban renewal strategy. Once completed, the upgraded traffic lights will reduce confusion, prevent accidents, and improve travel times—especially in Monze’s growing commercial zones.”

 

He further emphasized the importance of the site visits which he said were designed to help contractors understand the technical and logistical requirements, paving the way for competitive bidding and timely execution.

title.rendered: WATER AID ZAMBIA AND MONZE COUNCIL LAUNCH SUSTAINABILITY DRIVE FOR WASH INFRASTRUCTURE

content.rendered:
In a concerted effort to fortify long-term access to clean water and sanitation, Water Aid Zambia and Monze District Council convened a two-day planning meeting aimed at developing a robust sustainability plan for Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) infrastructure.

 

The initiative was supported by the ongoing Drought and Cholera Response Project and brought together technical experts, local authorities, and community representatives.

 

“This meeting was meant to ensure sustainability of the infrastructure being developed,” said Mr. Tassel Bulanda, Water Aid’s Southern Province Manager, as he officially closed the gathering.

 

He emphasized the significance of embedding community voices into the sustainability roadmap, which is expected to guide activities into 2026 and serve as a tool for lobbying and resource mobilization.

 

Mr. Bulanda noted that the plan would utilize both local authority funds and support from cooperating partners within the district.

 

“It’s not just about technical input. We have engaged the communities to ensure their voices shape this document. It’s a tool for collective accountability and sustainability,” he said.

 

And Mr. Bulanda explained Water Aid’s contributions in Monze District have included the construction of more than 31 water networks, maternity annexes, and numerous hand washing facilities.

 

He said the installations which are now under the stewardship of communities and the local authority, underscore a shift toward local ownership and sustained engagement.

 

“We are Constructing a new water network with three water kiosks under the Drought and Cholera Response Project at Bbolomani, well upgrades at Manungu, Makonka and Mulongalwili Health Centres, with solar-powered piped water systems, modern ablution blocks, and handwashing stations will also be done.”

 

Another core component across all sites involves hygiene promotion and the training of WASH Committees to strengthen maintenance, awareness, and sustainability practices.

 

He further said Water Aid Zambia envisions that the success of the sustainability planning model will serve as a blueprint for replication across other districts.

 

He said the he initiative represents a strategic step forward in strengthening rural public health and infrastructure resilience in the face of climate shocks and disease outbreaks.

 

The meeting was attended by stakeholders from World Vision, Southern Water and Sewerage Company (SWASCO), the District Education Board Secretary (DEBS) office, the local authority, and other community-based partners.

title.rendered: MONZE STEPS UP WASH EFFORTS: D-WASHE PLATFORM URGED TO DRIVE COORDINATION AND SUSTAINABILITY

content.rendered:
In an effort to enhance coordination and sustainability in the Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) sector, Acting Monze Town Council Secretary Mr. Oscar Chilanga has called on local stakeholders and development partners to intensify collaboration through the District Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Education (D-WASHE) Committee platform.

 

Speaking during the official opening of a two-day engagement meeting hosted by Water Aid Zambia at the Monze Civic Centre, Mr. Chilanga highlighted pressing challenges in the district, including widespread water scarcity, inadequate sanitation facilities, and poor hygiene education.

 

“Access to clean and safe drinking water remains a significant challenge in many communities. Families continue to rely on contaminated sources, and the health repercussions are devastating,” he stated.

 

The D-WASHE Committee, a multi-stakeholder body, is mandated to align district-level WASH efforts with national frameworks such as the National Urban and Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Programs.

 

Mr. Chilanga emphasized the need for active participation from Ward Development Committees (WDCs) in identifying community-driven projects eligible for support through the Constituency Development Fund (CDF).

 

He stressed that routing applications through WDCs and encouraging community ownership would promote continuity and local stewardship of WASH infrastructure.

 

Commending development partners for introducing sustainable innovations—including solar-powered water pumps, rainwater harvesting systems, and ecological sanitation solutions—Mr. Chilanga noted that these approaches are shaping the district’s broader sustainability strategy.

 

He also applauded the impact of community-led models that empower residents to manage and maintain water systems independently.

 

“This is not just about infrastructure—it’s about dignity, health, and the future of our communities. Let us deliberate freely and develop a clear plan to ensure our WASH solutions last,” Mr. Chilanga urged.

 

The event drew participation from key WASH actors, including representatives from World Vision, Southern Water and Sewerage Company (SWASCO), the District Education Board Secretary’s (DEBS) office, the local authority, Zambia National Service (ZNS) and several community-based organizations.

 

Discussions during the training focused on identifying operational gaps, sharing practical experiences, and proposing sustainable solutions to enhance WASH service delivery.

 

Participants also highlighted successes such as the active role of community water committees and increased leadership from traditional authorities in promoting hygiene behavior change.

 

The two-day engagement reaffirmed Monze District’s commitment to inclusive, community-driven solutions that strengthen WASH infrastructure and safeguard public health.

title.rendered: Local Government Service Commission Concludes Visit to Monze Town Council with Focus on Staffing and Financial Challenges

content.rendered:
Monze, Zambia – Tuesday

A delegation from the Local Government Service Commission, led by Commissioner Margaret Kapiya, concluded a working visit to Monze Town Council on Tuesday, during which a series of high-level meetings were held to address critical staffing and financial matters affecting the district.

The visit kicked off with a courtesy call on Monze District Commissioner Mwanza Malambo, who passionately advocated for the promotion of long-serving council officers with strong performance records. He emphasized the need to recognize institutional experience by prioritizing internal promotions before recruiting new staff, noting this would not only boost morale but also ensure that experienced officers help mentor junior personnel.

“We appreciate the Commission’s support in boosting our human resource base,” said Mr. Malambo, adding that continuity and mentorship are vital for maintaining service delivery standards amid expanding responsibilities.

Commissioner Kapiya reaffirmed the purpose of the recruitment exercise, stating it was aimed at strengthening local authorities in response to the growing workload brought about by increased Constituency Development Fund (CDF) allocations. She further disclosed that the Commission was conducting a staff audit to identify gaps and recommend appropriate reinforcements.

The visiting team also held discussions with Council Chairperson Powell Muntenguna, who raised the alarm over the swelling wage bill at the local authority. Mr. Muntenguna expressed concern that the Local Government Equalization Fund was insufficient to cover the financial burden created by recent staff additions, and called for an upward review of the fund.

“Our locally generated revenue is unable to sustain the wage demands. It’s straining operations and choking the council’s ability to deliver services,” said Mr. Muntenguna.

In response, Commissioner Kapiya encouraged Monze Town Council to explore alternative revenue streams. She reminded stakeholders that the council, as a corporate entity, holds the capacity to undertake entrepreneurial ventures beyond the traditional dependence on levies.

Later, during an engagement with council workers, Commissioner Kapiya underscored the weight of responsibility shouldered by public servants. She urged them to uphold professionalism and address the recurring audit queries through diligence and accountability in their day-to-day functions.

The visit comes at a pivotal moment for local authorities across Zambia, as the devolution of resources through CDF continues to place heightened demands on councils to deliver with efficiency, transparency, innovation and accountability.

title.rendered: Local Government Service Commission Commends Monze District for Exceptional Execution of CDF Projects

content.rendered:
Monze, Zambia — A delegation from the Local Government Service Commission (LGSC), led by Commissioner Maggie Kapihya, has lauded Monze District’s remarkable strides in implementing projects under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), citing the District as a model of effective local governance and community engagement.

The high-level delegation, which included Commissioner Barnabas Chiiya and several senior staff members from the Commission, toured projects across Monze Central and Bweengwa Constituencies in a two-day working visit aimed at evaluating progress and ensuring accountability in public service delivery.

“We are deeply encouraged by what we have seen. The commitment of the district’s officers and their alignment with the needs of the people truly reflects the vision of the CDF — to bring development closer to communities and uplift livelihoods at the grassroots.” stated Commissioner Kapihya.

The projects visited spanned key sectors including education, health, and infrastructure, such as classroom blocks, health posts, dams, and road rehabilitation works in Monze Central and Bweengwa Constituencies — all funded through the CDF allocation.

Monze Town Council Secretary Beston Kajoba confirmed that all planned 2024 CDF projects had been initiated and the majority were already completed, with a few awaiting formal handover within the next two weeks.

He emphasized that the local authority is committed to delivering 2025 projects well before year-end to maintain momentum and eliminate the risk of project rollovers into 2026.

“We are focused on timely execution, quality assurance, and ensuring no community is left behind,” Mr. Kajoba noted, adding that continued collaboration with oversight bodies like the LGSC was key to sustaining progress.

Meanwhile Commissioner Chiiya also took the opportunity to reaffirm the Commission’s support through strategic staff deployment to local authorities, boosting human resource capacity to better respond to increased administrative demands resulting from decentralization reforms.

The visit served was not only a monitoring mission but also as a platform for dialogue between commission officials, council staff, and district leaders—fostering transparency, feedback, and shared ownership of developmental goals.

As Zambia deepens its decentralization agenda, Monze District’s performance under the CDF is emerging as a testament to the transformative power of local governance when paired with accountability, civic engagement, and dedicated leadership.

Monze District Marks World Environment Day with a Call to End Plastic Pollution

content.rendered:
Monze District joined the rest of the world in commemorating World Environment Day on Thursday afternoon, with a strong call to end plastic pollution and embrace sustainable environmental practices.

The event, held at Manungu Secondary School, brought together government officials, educators, and community members to champion the cause of environmental conservation.

Speaking on behalf of Monze Town Council Chairman, Deputy Chairman Abel Hachaambwa emphasized the urgent need for collective action against plastic pollution.

He urged schools to collaborate with traditional leaders in fostering a culture of recycling and adopting biodegradable alternatives.

Mr. Hachaambwa stressed that plastic pollution is not merely an eyesore but a crisis impacting human health, wildlife, and water sources, as well as clogging drainage systems and contaminating soil.

“Plastic pollution is a serious environmental threat that requires a mindset change among our people. We must move towards sustainable solutions such as recycling and the use of biodegradable materials,” Hachaambwa said.

To the marketeers whom he described as the backbone of the local economy, Mr. Hachaambwa encouraged them to explore eco-friendly packaging options and reduce reliance on single-use plastics.

He called on various stakeholders—including the Government, community members, and organizations—to serve as agents of change in safeguarding the environment for future generations.

Meanwhile, Monze Town Council Secretary Beston Kajoba, speaking on behalf of the District Commissioner, underscored the importance of commemorating environmental awareness days, particularly in light of climate change challenges.

He referenced the devastating drought experienced during the 2023/2024 farming season as a stark reminder of the urgency of environmental preservation.

title.rendered: K2.4 Million Empowerment Boost for Moomba Constituency: 145 Clubs Receive Funding

content.rendered:
Monze—Monze Town Council on Tuesday officially disbursed K2.4 million under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), benefiting 145 women and youth clubs across Moomba Constituency.
The grant, which follows a rigorous application and selection process, comes as part of the government’s broader commitment to inclusive growth and equitable resource distribution.
Out of the 256 applications received, 145 clubs were approved for funding, while those that did not make the cut this year have been assured priority in the next allocation cycle.
Speaking at the handover ceremony held in Nabukuyu on Tuesday afternoon, Moomba Constituency Member of Parliament Fred Chatila reaffirmed the government’s dedication to fostering socio-economic advancement.

He further assured unsuccessful applicants that they would be prioritized in subsequent disbursements, reinforcing a fair and equitable approach to empowerment grants.
Hon. Chatila further issued a stern warning against individuals who repeatedly submit applications under different club names in an attempt to secure funding year after year saying “such actions disadvantage other deserving groups that genuinely need support for their initiatives.”
Echoing these sentiments, Monze Town Council Chairman Powell Mutenguna urged beneficiaries to use the funds strictly for their intended purpose.
He emphasized that misallocation of resources not only disrupts development plans but also undermines the integrity of the empowerment program.
“These funds have been allocated based on clear objectives. Beneficiaries must ensure that they follow through with their proposed projects, creating sustainable impact in their communities,” Mutenguna advised.
The empowerment grants come at a time when local communities are pushing for greater transparency in the administration of CDF resources.
Government officials and council representatives have pledged to closely monitor the implementation of projects funded under this scheme to ensure accountability and measurable outcomes.

title.rendered: 36.32M Monze Central, Bweengwa Community Projects and Bursaries Granted

content.rendered:
Monze – May 21, 2025 –

Monze Town Council has been given a go ahead to implement community projects amounting to a cumulative total of K36.32 Million for the completion of phased projects and new community projects, climate resilience programs, and secondary school bursaries under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) for Bweengwa and Monze Central Constituencies for the 2025 CDF funding.

Provincial Local Government Officer Mr. Mainza Sikaale granted the approvals, marking a significant step in local development efforts for the two Constituencies.

The approved allocations for Bweengwa Constituency include K5.91 million for completion of phased community projects and K11.49 million for new initiatives.

Additionally, Mr. Sikaale approved the funds allocated for the purchase of a solar system at Hamangaba Rural Health Centre from the 2024 CDF allocation in Hamangaba ward.

The bursary program will support 191 returning pupils at a total cost of K631,440, while two new applicants will receive K6,000 in funding bringing the combined total to K637,440.

Speaking on the development, Monze Town Council Public Relations Officer Kanchele Kanchele emphasized the importance of transparency and efficiency in fund utilization.

“This approval marks a crucial step in ensuring that development projects and educational support reach the intended beneficiaries. As a local authority we are committed to maintaining accountability and ensuring that all funds are disbursed through the proper channels,” said Kanchele.

For Monze Central Constituency, the approved allocations include K8.78 million to complete phased community projects from 2023 and 2024 as K9.41 million has been set aside for new 2025 community projects, while K900,950 for additional climate resilience projects from the 2024 CDF allocation.

Additionally, extra resources have been approved for the rehabilitation of a classroom block at Mulongalwili Primary School which was damaged in 2024 due to extreme weather under the 2025 disaster component.

The approval also outlined key conditions for implementation, including strict adherence to procurement regulations, monitoring and evaluation programs, and quarterly reporting to stakeholders.

Mr. Kanchele further highlighted the need for increased sensitization on CDF opportunities.

“We encourage community members to engage actively in these projects and take advantage of the available resources. The council will continue working closely with stakeholders to ensure effective implementation,” he added.

With the approval in place, Monze Town Council is set to begin the execution of these projects, reinforcing its commitment to community development and educational empowerment.

title.rendered: MTC HOSTS VALIDATION MEETING ON NEW 2024 CDF GUIDELINES

content.rendered:
Monze Town Council successfully hosted a stakeholders meeting to review, sensitize and validate the newly revised Constituency Development Fund (CDF) Guidelines in line with the 2024 Act for Monze Central Constituency.

The meeting was held with the aim of ensuring that all relevant parties are well-informed about the updated procedures and standards governing the administration of the CDF.

The presentation was led by Monze Town Council Secretary Mr. Beston Kajoba, Director of Planning Ms. Maria Mwandalesa, and Mr. Munenga Gupira from the Community Development Unity.

In attendance were members from Monze Town Council who facilitated the meeting,  Monze Central Constituency Development Fund  Committee, Ward Development Committee members from Monze Central wards, Community Leaders, and various stakeholders from the Constituency.

Monze Council Secretary Beston Kajoba emphasized on the clarity and structure provided by the new guidelines, which apply not just to Monze but across all constituencies.

He said while the core components of the CDF remain unchanged, the updated guidelines provide a more defined framework for implementation, especially in the administration of Bursaries, Empowerments – Loans and Grants.

He stressed the importance of correctly identifying and supporting vulnerable individuals and communities to ensure equitable access to CDF resources and effective utilization of the funds in order to improve the livelihoods of our people in our communities.

The criteria for loan eligibility have been clearly outlined, with a focus on transparency and accountability in the disbursement process.

It was also noted that the CDF system has not changed, maintaining consistency and emphasizing the evaluation of applications and project proposals by the technical appraisal committees.

The sensitization meeting served as an important platform to promote awareness and encourage collaborative implementation of the CDF, ensuring that development initiatives meet the needs of the communities they are intended to serve.

Moomba and Bweengwa Constituencies will have their own validation meetings in their Constituencies at venues which are centrally located to ensure high participation from stakeholders in their areas.

title.rendered: COMMUNITY SECURITY BOOSTED WITH COMMISSIONING OF CHIKUNI AND BWEENGWA POLICE STATIONS

content.rendered:
Chikuni and Bweengwa Police Stations have been officially commissioned, marking a new chapter in the fight against rising criminal activities in the District.

The Chikuni Police Station, constructed at a cost of K2.8 million, was officially inaugurated on Wednesday.

The project began on March 23, 2023, amid growing concerns over increasing crime rates, particularly incidents of stock theft and murder linked to witchcraft accusations.

In his address at the commissioning ceremony, Minister of Home Affairs and Internal Security, Jack Mwiimbu SC, expressed his optimism that the establishment of the police station would serve as a deterrent to crime in the area.

“The community should feel a renewed sense of security with the presence of this police station,” he stated.

Hon. Mwiimbu urged residents to collaborate closely with law enforcement to ensure safety and security in their neighborhoods.

Echoing the minister’s sentiments, Auxensio Daka, Southern Province Commissioner of Police, representing the Inspector General of Police, called on the local community to actively participate in maintaining peace.

“Please report unlawful activities rather than resorting to self-resolution,” he urged, emphasizing the critical role of community cooperation in effective law enforcement.

On Tuesday Hon. Mwiimbu SC commissioned Bweengwa Police Station.

The facility, which cost over K6 million, includes three staff houses and an ablution block that are yet to be completed.

The project also commenced on March 23, 2023, reflecting the government’s commitment to strengthening police infrastructure in response to public safety concerns.

At the Bweengwa commissioning event on Tuesday afternoon, Minister Mwiimbu reiterated the importance of utilizing the new facility for addressing criminal offences legally.

“Do not take the law into your own hands; let this police station be a sanctuary for justice and support,” he implored.

Also present at the ceremony was Bweengwa Constituency Member of Parliament, Michelo Kasauta, who emphasized the need for the officers at the new police station to adhere to high professional standards in their duty of protecting and serving the community.

The commissioning of these police stations marks a pivotal step towards improving security and fostering trust between law enforcement and the community in Monze District, as both residents and officials look forward to a safer environment.

title.rendered: MONZE TOWN COUNCIL REPORTS IMPROVED SERVICE DELIVERY AFTER DEVOLUTION

content.rendered:
Monze Town Council Secretary Beston Kajoba reported that the devolution of certain functions to local authorities has significantly enhanced service delivery in the district, despite some initial challenges.

Speaking when he made presentation before the Parliamentary Committee on Local Governance, Housing, and Chiefs’ Affairs meeting held in Mazabuka on Thursday, Mr. Kajoba emphasized that the devolved functions have largely run smoothly, noting that the improvements in operations are evident in the outputs that the local authority was able to deliver last year under the devolved functions.

“We raised K200,000.00 from livestock and fisheries, which we reinvested into purchasing motorbikes for use by camp officers and computers as well for service provisions,” he stated as he highlighted the positive impact of local revenue generation on operational capacity.

Mr. Kajoba acknowledged the presence of “teething problems,” particularly regarding the receipt of funds lacking proper descriptions for easy allocation given the fact all devolved functions are funded through a single Sector Grant account. He further highlighted office accommodation as another challenge among others.

He however, assured the committee members that these issues are being addressed progressively, allowing for continued enhancements in service delivery in a decentralized system.

Chairperson of the Committee, Hon. Twaambo Mutinta, MP for Itezhi Tezhi, supported Mr. Kajoba’s observations, stressing that devolution aims to improve efficiency within local governance rather than undermine established structures.

He challenged officers involved in devolved functions to accept and act on the directives from two Cabinet memorandums, urging them to move beyond resistance to change.

“We are aware of officers resisting change,” Hon. Mutinta remarked, calling for strengthened collaboration with Council Secretaries and Town Clerks to ensure the success of the devolution process.

His comments highlighted a commitment to fostering cooperation and responsiveness among local governance bodies.

The committee’s engagement included representatives from Mazabuka Municipal Council, Monze, Chikankata, and Gwembe Town Councils.

The primary objective of the meeting was to gather insights regarding the ongoing devolution process, assess challenges faced by the councils, and explore recommendations to enhance local governance.

Each council presented specific challenges related to resource allocation and the need for capacity building, underscoring the importance of adequate support for devolved entities to fulfill their functions effectively.

Additionally, Hon. Mutinta indicated that MPs are in agreement about finding ways to empower Ward Development Committees (WDCs), recognizing their critical role in local development efforts.

This meeting reflects the ongoing efforts to enhance local governance in Zambia, as councils adapt to the changes brought about by decentralization through devolution and work toward more effective service delivery for their communities.

title.rendered: CONSTITUENCY DEVELOPMENT FUND: A CATALYST FOR CHANGE IN MONZE CENTRAL

content.rendered:
Chikuni, Monze -Amid the hustle and bustle of the Charles Lwanga Market area in Chikuni, a symphony of mechanical sounds filled the air as road maintenance machinery orchestrated a reminder of progress and development. This scene unfolded as road maintenance machines made their way back to their base at Monze Town Council after completing a significant project on the 10.2 KM Singonya-Mulongalwili Road.

The commotion attracted the interest of local marketers who gathered by the roadside to witness the machines, a sign of hope for improved connectivity in their community. Among the onlookers was a woman conversing in the local dialect who proudly proclaimed that these machines were a testament to the power of the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), purchased for the benefit of Monze Central residents.

Road Improvements and Economic Opportunities

The visit from the Director of Works and Engineering Services was part of a broader routine check on projects funded by the CDF, highlighting the government’s commitment to infrastructural development. The machines, now temporarily resting, provided an opportunity for local residents to reflect on the broader implications of such projects.

“I express my gratitude to the local authority for the work done on the road,” said Cabin Haanyika a canter driver who stopped to pick up drinks. His voice rang with optimism as he noted that improved road infrastructure would not only facilitate smoother transportation for goods but also bolster local businesses and service delivery.

With the agricultural sector thriving, drivers and locals alike shared their anticipation of a bumper harvest, recognizing with relief that transporting produce to the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) sheds would no longer pose a logistical nightmare. Precedence Moomba, a teacher from Mulongalwili, echoed these sentiments, suggesting that the completion of the Singonya-Mulongalwili road would ease the traveling woes that had plagued the community for years.

Beyond Roads: Transforming Lives

The rapid testimonials from road users exemplify the multifaceted impact of the Constituency Development Fund on the local community. The CDF is playing a critical role in not just enhancing road connectivity but also facilitating numerous developmental projects that touch the lives of residents.

In addition to roads, the Fund has been pivotal in constructing classroom blocks, establishing maternity annexes, and developing water reticulation facilities. Furthermore, it has empowered local entrepreneurs through grants and loans, enhancing economic opportunities and fostering a spirit of self-reliance within the constituency. It would be de-service if the list left out the Bursary schemes for Skills and Secondary which are playing a pivotal role in ensuring that children remain in school regardless of the financial constraints of their guardians.

Future of Development in Monze Central

The sense of ownership among residents, particularly regarding the machinery used for road works, underscores a growing awareness and appreciation for the CDF’s role in fostering community development. It is a potent reminder that local voices matter in the discourse of development; the acknowledgment of the residents’ contributions to these initiatives does not go unnoticed.

As the sun set over Chikuni, casting golden hues across the market, it became evident that the initiatives funded by the Constituency Development Fund are more than just infrastructure projects; they symbolize hope, resilience, and a collective effort towards sustainable community growth.

With ongoing projects and the promise of more to come, Monze Central is poised for a transformation that likely extends far beyond its borders, demonstrating that well-allocated public funds can indeed pave the way for a brighter future.

In the end, development is not merely about the construction of roads or buildings—it’s about building communities, enhancing lives, and fostering prosperity for generations to come. As residents of Monze Central look to the future, they are not just witnessing change; they are active participants in crafting their destiny, empowered by initiatives like the Constituency Development Fund.

title.rendered: BWEENGWA CONSTITUENCY DEVELOPMENT FUND COMMITTEE SET TO HAND OVER KEY INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS

content.rendered:
Monze, 19/03/25 – The Bweengwa Constituency Development Fund (CDF) committee is preparing to officially hand over several key infrastructure projects funded by the CDF, marking a significant milestone in the community’s development efforts.

The projects range from educational facilities to essential health and water services, showcasing the New Dawn Government’s commitment to enhancing the living standards and resilience of local communities.

Among the standout projects is a new semi-detached house for Ganda Primary School, constructed by the local construction company, Womentech Investment Limited, at a cost of K920,000.

This school housing project aims to provide a conducive environment for teachers and improve their retention, ultimately benefiting the students’ educational experience.

In addition to the educational facility, the committee has constructed essential infrastructure at Muthamzhi Rural Center, including a staff house for healthcare workers, an ablution block, and a water reticulation facility.

These enhancements are designed to improve the living conditions for staff and enhance service delivery in the healthcare sector.

Chunga Rural Center will also see significant developments with the completion of key projects. The community is set to receive a staff house, ablution block, and water reticulation facilities, all of which are scheduled to be handed over to the local council shortly.

These projects are expected to address the pressing needs of the community by providing vital amenities that promote hygiene and better health care access.

Further, the CDF committee is excited to announce the handover of several climate-resistant initiatives. These projects aim to prepare the community for the adverse effects of climate change, ensuring sustainable living conditions for current and future residents as well as ensuring that livestock is preserved when the region experiences drought such as that of 2023-24 season.

By focusing on climate resilience, the committee underscores its commitment to not only addressing immediate infrastructural needs but also nurturing a sustainable future for the constituency.

The handover ceremony is anticipated to attract local leaders, community members, and partners who have supported the development initiatives. The CDF committee sees this event as an opportunity to showcase the tangible benefits of community-driven projects and to foster a sense of ownership among residents.

“The successful completion of these projects represents a significant step forward in the New Dawn Government’s commitment to developing not only Bweengwa Constituency but Monze District as whole. Government believes that these infrastructure improvements will have a lasting impact on our community’s quality of life, particularly in education, health, and environmental resilience,” said Kanchele Kanchele the Public Relations Officer at the local authority.

“As the Bweengwa community prepares to celebrate these achievements, the local authority urges all residents to embrace the newly completed facilities and take active roles in maintaining them for future generations. The projects are more than just buildings; they symbolize hope, progress, and a brighter future for all residents in the Bweengwa constituency and Monze District,” he said.

title.rendered: Technical Assistance Model for School Health Program Launched in Monze

content.rendered:
Technical Assistance Model for School Health Program Launched in Monze

Monze District, 05/03/2025 – The Ministry of Education, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and partners such as Healthy Learners, officially launched the Technical Assistance Model for the School Health Program, marking a significant step forward in improving health care and education access for students.

The event was graced by Acting Council Secretary Oscar Chilanga, who read a statement on behalf of Council Chairperson Powell Muntenguna.

In his remarks, Mr. Chilanga expressed gratitude to the Ministry of Education for the opportunity to participate in the launch and emphasized the importance of collaboration between education and health sectors. “Together, we are showing our mandate to promote education and health coverage for all,” he highlighted.

The School Health Program is described as a transformative initiative aimed at ensuring students receive necessary health care benefits that support their academic engagement and long-term societal contributions.

“This move will ensure the program lives beyond a specified time frame,” Mr. Chilanga stated, underscoring the commitment of local authorities to prioritize health and education in the community.

Mr. Chilanga also took the opportunity to call on stakeholders, including District Education Board Secretaries (DEBS) and community members, to utilize the Constituency Development Fund to expand the School Health Program in Monze district.

He asserted that such expansions will enhance the infrastructure of local schools and provide essential healthcare facilities, improving the overall well-being and academic performance of learners.

And speaking on behalf of health learners vice president for government engagement, the organization’s Advocate Coordinator Bertha Chulu noted that, this program aims to benefit learners across the country.

title.rendered: HAAMPONGO BRIDGE CONSTRUCTION COMMENCE

content.rendered:
Monze, 28/01/2025 – A wave of excitement is sweeping through the Haampongo and Mulongalwili communities in Singonya Ward as construction has commenced on a much-needed bridge across the Haampongo stream.

This long-awaited project promises to significantly improve the lives of residents by easing access to essential services, education, and markets.

For years, residents have faced the daunting challenge of navigating the often-impassable stream, which has severely hampered their daily lives.

However, with the construction of this new bridge, a brighter future beckons.

“We are overjoyed that this bridge is finally being built,” shared one resident. “It will make a huge difference in our daily lives.”

Mwiinga Maxwell of Haampongo expressed his profound gratitude to the New Dawn Government for this crucial project.

“We have a shed at Singonya which supplies maize to communities in Mulongalwili, Kalisowe and Nakabwe who use this road, and this bridge will help in easing the movement,” he explained.

“And also, our children who go to Mulongalwili school find it difficult when it rains. We are very grateful to the council, the New Dawn Government, and our local leaders.”

Admore Mwiinga echoed his colleague’s sentiments, emphasizing the bridge’s vital role in improving access to essential services for the people in the area.

Trinity Hardware and Construction Company has been contracted to undertake the project at a cost of K1.3 million.

The company has assured residents of a durable and long-lasting bridge, with completion expected within four months.

The Singonya Ward Councilor Chandrine Kaaba echoed the sentiments of the residents, stating, “This bridge will alleviate the immense difficulties we face in moving around. Farmers will easily transport their produce to markets, and accessing essential services like the Mulongalwili Clinic and Chikuni Mission will become much simpler.”

He highlighted the significant impact on education, noting that school children have suffered the most due to the treacherous stream crossings.

“In 2023, some children had to endure a 14-hour wait to cross the swollen stream before they could write their final exams. This bridge will finally put an end to such hardships.”

This bridge will not only serve the immediate communities of Haampongo and Mulongalwili but also benefit residents of Kalisowe, Nakabwe, and other surrounding areas.

As construction progresses, the excitement and gratitude among the residents continue to grow, with many anticipating a brighter future with improved connectivity and access to opportunities.

The Construction of new bridge at Haampongo stream was funded by 2024 Constituency Development Fund (CDF)

title.rendered: LUSANGU DAM REHABILITATION NEARS COMPLETION IN MONZE

content.rendered:
Monze, Southern Province – The long-awaited water for animals in Mwanza West Ward, located in Rusangu Zone is nearing completion as the rehabilitation of the Rusangu Dam is slated to be done in the next ten (10) days.

A community meeting was held at the site by Monze Town Council Chairperson, Powell Mutenguna, to appreciate the ongoing works.

The rehabilitation project, awarded to Nomiks General Dealers at a cost of K2,980,640.00 million, has seen significant local participation, with numerous local residents, including women, employed to carry out light physical works.

The Lusangu Dam, constructed in 1959, is being renovated under the 2024 Constituency Development Fund (CDF) budget. According to the Council Chairperson, Mr. Mutenguna, the project has progressed at a commendable rate, reaching 85% completion.

“We are hopeful that once completed, this project will significantly address the water challenges faced by the community,” said Mutenguna.

He further emphasized the importance of community involvement, urging residents to actively participate in community meetings to ensure their voices are heard in the selection and presentation of developmental projects.

Monze Town Council Director of Engineering Services Victor Mbaimbai said the rehabilitation project at a Lusangu dam is meant to ensure its long-term safety and efficiency.

He said the project scope includes a range of crucial measures aimed at improving the dam’s structural integrity and operational performance and serviceability to the wider community of the ward.

According to the Director of Engineering Services, the rehabilitation works encompass a comprehensive list of improvements, including: wingwall and headwall reinforcement, which means strengthening the structures that guide water flow towards and away the spillway. Implementing measures to prevent water seepage through the dam’s foundation by installation of seals.

Other works include increasing the height of the spillway by 0.3 meters to enhance its capacity to impound larger volumes of water during floods and improve the embankment gradient of the dam to mitigate soil erosion and maintain stability among others.

Recognizing the potential risks associated with the age of the dam, the Director of Engineering Services emphasized the importance of reinforcing the spillway to prevent potential failures.

“The plan involves incorporating buttresses into the spillways cross section. These structures will help to counteract the significant forces exerted by the static water pressure from the upstream side of the dam.

This rehabilitation project is crucial for ensuring the continued safety and serviceability of the dam, which plays a vital role in the local community. The project is expected to significantly enhance the dam’s resilience against future floods and other potential threats, such as breaching, thereby protecting surrounding properties and infrastructure,” he said.

Eng. Joseph Mubanga, Director of Nomiks General Dealers, confirmed that the project, which commenced in December 2024, is on schedule for completion by the end of January 2025. The rehabilitated dam will serve the water needs of animals in 22 villages within Mwanza West Ward.

The successful completion of the Lusangu Dam rehabilitation project will undoubtedly bring relief to the local community and improve the livelihoods of those dependent on livestock farming and sustenance.

title.rendered: MONZE DISBURSES OVER K15 MILLION TO 22,115 HOUSEHOLDS UNDER CASH FOR WORK

content.rendered:
Monze, Southern Province – Monze Town Council has disbursed a total of K15,669,624 to 22,115 households across the district under the government’s Cash for Work program.

The program, implemented to mitigate the impact of the 2023-2024 drought, has seen significant financial support distributed to communities in need.

Monze Central Constituency, with the highest number of zones (75), has received the largest share of the funds, with K7,772,460 disbursed to date.

Bweengwa Constituency follows closely with K5,596,199 distributed across its 50 zones. Moomba Constituency, with the fewest zones (27), has received K2,300,967.

The Cash for Work program is a crucial intervention by the New Dawn Government to provide temporary employment and income support to vulnerable households during times of economic hardship, such as droughts or other natural disasters. It aims to alleviate poverty, improve food security, and enhance community resilience.

Council Public Relations Officer Kanchele Kanchele confirmed that the figures represent disbursements up to November, with a few payments for that month still being processed.

He also stated that recruitment for December and January is currently underway, contingent on the timely receipt of funds from the government.

Mr. Kanchele explained that the program’s initial August start date was delayed to September due to logistical and training requirements.

The Cash for Work program plays a vital role in supporting vulnerable communities in Zambia. By providing employment opportunities and financial assistance, it helps to mitigate the impacts of drought shocks and empowers individuals and families to overcome hardship.

title.rendered: CHIBUYU POLICE POST IN MONZE TO BE REBUILT AFTER GASSING INCIDENT

content.rendered:
Monze – A sigh of relief has washed over residents of Site and Service in Monze’s Urban Ward as the long-awaited reconstruction of the Chibuyu Police Post has finally commenced.

The police post, tragically destroyed during the widespread gassing incidents of 2019, has been a glaring void in the community’s security infrastructure.

The Monze Central Constituency Development Fund Committee has taken a significant step towards addressing this critical gap by allocating substantial funds for the project.

This project will not only improve law enforcement capabilities but also serve as a visible deterrent to criminal activity. We are confident that this initiative will contribute to a substantial reduction in crime rates within the area and enhance the overall quality of life for our residents,” he said.

The project has been met with enthusiastic support from the local community and many residents have expressed their gratitude to the Monze Central Constituency Development Fund Committee for prioritizing this critical infrastructure need.

The residents believe that the reopening of the police post will not only improve their safety and security but also strengthen the bond between the community and law enforcement agencies.

As construction progresses, the community eagerly awaits the completion of the project and the return of a dedicated police presence to the area.

The rebuilding of the Chibuyu Police Post symbolizes a renewed commitment to community safety and a brighter future for the residents of Site and Service.

As more councils embrace the digital landscape, the potential for better resource management and community interaction continues to grow.

The significant increase in both expenditure and revenue projections reflects a strategic approach to address the pressing needs and priorities of the District.

title.rendered: CHIEF HAMUSONDE’S PALACE HANDOVER MARKS MILESTONE IN COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

content.rendered:
STORY BY KANCHELE JUNIOR

 Bweengwa Constituency, Monze District –A significant milestone was celebrated today with the handover of phase one of Chief Hamusonde’s Palace in Bweengwa Constituency, symbolizing the government’s commitment to enhancing the living conditions of traditional leaders and fostering community development.

The handover ceremony was attended by prominent figures including the Provincial Permanent Secretary for Southern Province, Dr Namani Monze, the District Commissioner, Mr. Mwanza Malambo, Council Chairperson Mr. Powell Mutenguna, The Council Secretary Mr. Beston Kajoba, Chief Chikanta, Chief Monze, Chief Chikuni and various traditional and local leaders.

In a speech read on his behalf by Dr. Monze, Southern Province Minister Hon. Credo Najuwa emphasized the importance of the Palace as more than just a building but that it serves as a monument to the strength, unity, and cultural heritage of the community.

Hon. Najuwa acknowledged the dedication of the Monze Town Council, praising their relentless commitment to development in Bweengwa Constituency and Monze District.

title.rendered: CASH FOR WORK PROGRAMME LAUNCHED IN MONZE DISTRICT TO COMBAT HUNGER

content.rendered:
Monze District, Zambia – In a significant step towards alleviating hunger among the poorest communities, District Commissioner Mwanza Malambo officially launched the Cash for Work (CFW) program on Wednesday at Malundu Secondary School.

The initiative aims to provide financial support to vulnerable households while promoting community engagement and development.

During the launch, Mr. Malambo emphasized the New Dawn Government’s commitment to ensuring that no one in Zambia suffers from hunger.

He stated, “President Hakainde Hichilema has clearly outlined that no one will die from hunger, and through initiatives like the Cash for Work program, we are actively working to support those in need.”

The CFW program is designed to target the most vulnerable members of the community, which Mr. Malambo noted that not everyone would benefit from the initiative and that the focus on the poorest underscores the Government’s intent to prioritize those who are most in need.

And Mr. Powell Mutenguna, the Council Chairperson of Monze District, echoed these sentiments, highlighting the challenges of limited resources.

He appealed for community support and understanding, urging residents to be sympathetic towards vulnerable households.

“We must ensure transparency in identifying rightful beneficiaries. We are calling on traditional leaders to facilitate community meetings to foster inclusivity and avoid accusations of unfairness in the selection process,” he said.

The head teacher of Malundu Secondary School William Kwibisa presented an initiative aimed at enhancing local agricultural practices.

He said the school is set to embark on a production unit project that will serve as an educational platform for community members.

He explained that the he project aims to demonstrate efficient food production techniques on small plots of land, ultimately contributing to food security in the community.

“To kick start the production unit project, the school will require assistance from the community, particularly in constructing a fence around the school garden. We are optimistic that this collaboration would lead to valuable knowledge transfer and empower local residents to improve their agricultural practices,” he said.

The launch event was attended by a diverse group of stakeholders, including Council Secretary Beston Kajoba, Malundu ward councilor, Local Government officials, representatives from various Government Departments, and traditional leaders.

As the Cash for Work program takes off, it represents a crucial effort by the Zambian Government to address hunger and promote sustainable development through community involvement and support. One thousand seven hundred and thirty-one (1731) vulnerable households will benefit from the CFW initiative in Monze District.

Monze Town Council Public Relations Officer Kanchele Kanchele says the Local Authority in collaboration with Chakamu Construction Company, is set to complete the highly anticipated works on the Nabukuyu-Moomba road.

title.rendered: Local Women’s Clubs in Monze Central Constituency Thriving with Government Support

content.rendered:
Story By Kanchele Kanchele

Local Women’s Clubs in Monze Central Constituency Thriving with Government Support
Monze Central Constituency, Women’s clubs and cooperatives in Monze Central Constituency have experienced significant growth and success thanks to the government’s support and grants. In total, K2, 150,000.00 was disbursed to 144 clubs and cooperatives, resulting in flourishing economic activities and improved livelihoods for the members.
One of the successful clubs is the Mukamba Wangu Women’s Club in Chipembele Ward, led by Chair Lady Astridah Hamwalengwa. The club received K15,000 and decided to invest in goat rearing. The decision proved fruitful as they now have a steady income source, benefiting the entire homestead.
Similarly, the Liso Women’s Club in Mayaba Ward, chaired by Lillian Hiimonde, utilized their grant of K15,000 to purchase 43 goats. With over 70 goats now in their possession, the members have expressed their desire to venture into dairy farming. Apart from supporting their livelihoods, the income generated from the club activities has also helped them pay school fees.
A recent sample survey carried out by the Monze Council, focusing on five wards including Mayaba, Chipembele, Singonya, Ufwenuka, and Chisekesi, showcased positive growth among the women’s clubs. Several economic activities such as poetry, piggery, and gardening were pursued by these clubs, resulting in prosperity and progress.
One area of concern highlighted by the clubs was the need for irrigation equipment. Regina Hangale, a member of the Katutonka Women’s Club in Singonya Ward, emphasized the importance of investing in irrigation projects, especially considering the current dry spell. The clubs have urged the local authorities to extend their support in procuring irrigation equipment, enabling them to diversify into irrigation farming.
The success stories of these women’s clubs are a testament to the government’s commitment to empowering women and fostering economic development at the grassroots level. The grants provided have proved instrumental in enabling these clubs to embark on various income-generating activities, leading to improved livelihoods and financial independence.
As the Monze Central Constituency continues to thrive, it is hoped that the government will continue extending its support to other women’s clubs and cooperatives, fostering sustainable growth and development in the region

title.rendered: ZAMBIA TAKES STEPS TOWARDS DECENTRALIZATION WITH $70 MILLION INVESTMENT IN TOWN  COUNCILS

content.rendered:
Story By KANCHELE KANCHELE

Public Relations Officer

14/02/24

MONZE-In a bid to accelerate the implementation of decentralization plans, the Zambia Devolution Support Services and officials from the Ministries of Local Government and Rural Development as well as Finance and National Planning held a meeting on Wednesday with Monze Town Council Management and Heads of Devolved Departments.

Speaking when he made his presentation to the Heads of Departments and Local Authority officials Zambia Devolution Support Program (ZDSP) Development Financial Management Specialist Kennedy Kazinga said the purpose of the meeting was to offer technical support services to ensure the successful execution of the decentralization plan, which was launched by Republican President, Hakainde Hichilema, on June 30th, 2023.

Central to the discussions was the allocation of $70 million grants to the 96 town councils for capital projects.

Mr. Kalinga explained that the financial support will be provided over a period of five years, with the first two years receiving $25 million in each year and the remaining three years receiving $45 million in each year.

He said the disbursement of these funds will be contingent upon councils meeting certain minimum conditions, which will determine their eligibility to receive a minimum of $200,000 in each of the first two years, and $500,000 in the following three years in each year.

“Crucially, councils that qualify for the funds will have the autonomy to choose projects that will benefit the public. However, these projects must be completed within the specified timeframe and adhere to quality, environmental, and social safeguards. The expectation is that the implemented projects should be sustainable and supported by all stakeholders,” he said.

During the meeting, it was emphasized that the prudent utilization of these funds will result in the development of high-quality infrastructure.

He said the investment is an opportunity for the 96 qualifying town councils across the country to make significant improvements to their respective areas.

The introduction of decentralization plans underscores President Hakainde Hichilema’s commitment to devolving power and resources to local authorities. This move is seen as a vital step in ensuring efficient service delivery, promoting local development, and empowering communities.

With the necessary financial support and technical assistance provided by the Zambia Devolution Support Services and Ministry of Finance and Planning Officials, it is hoped that the decentralization implementation plan, championed by President Hichilema, will be effectively achieved in Monze District.

The Local Authority has met the conditions set for 2022 and 2023 making it eligible to receive US $400,000.00.

title.rendered: Decentralisation Sensitisation Team Visits Monze: Urges Civil Servants Not To Be Stumbling Block In The Implementation Process

content.rendered:
Monze, 16/08/23
The decentralisation sensitisation team, led by Dr Peter Mumba, Chairperson of the Civil Service Commission, visited Monze on Tuesday afternoon.
Accompanied by senior civil servants, union leaders from the local authority and civil service, the team held a meeting to discuss the importance of decentralisation and its impact on government policies and service delivery.
During the meeting, Mr Peter Mumba emphasized that decentralisation is a long-term strategy by the government to bring power and resources closer to the people as well as empowering local communities and improving governance at the grassroots level.
He said decentralisation is here to stay, as it is the key to ensuring effective governance and promoting the welfare of the citizens.
Mr Mumba further highlighted the essential role of civil servants in the development process and acknowledged that civil servants are the key implementers of the policies formulated by politicians.
He explained that the dedication and commitment of civil servants to translating policies into tangible outcomes are crucial for the successful implementation of development programs.
Mr Mumba urged civil servants not to become stumbling blocks in the process but rather to actively support and contribute to the goals of decentralisation.
He observed that the allocation of resources to districts under decentralisation of resources through increased allocation of resources to Districts has raised expectations among the public and that people are hopeful that these resources will lead to improved service delivery and development initiatives in their respective areas.
In addition to Mr Mumba’s address, Milambo Mwakabantu Moonga, Assistant Director of the Public Service Management Division (PSMD), announced that new structures will be created in Councils to accommodate devolved departments.
She said this move aims to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of local government in meeting the needs and aspirations of the people.
Furthermore, Morgan Malambo, Director of Recruitment and Placement at PSMD, highlighted the financial challenges faced by Councils which he said would not sustain the 51,000 workers attached to them.
He observed that sustaining the salaries of these workers solely through council revenues is not feasible as a result, the workers will remain under the Payroll Management and Establishment Control (PMEC).
The meeting concluded with a call for cooperation among all stakeholders to work together in delivering quality services to the people.
As the decentralisation sensitisation team continues its efforts, it is expected that the visit to Monze and similar engagements will create awareness and understanding of the benefits and challenges of decentralisation.
It is hoped that these discussions will lead to the implementation of effective strategies to address any obstacles and ensure the successful realisation of decentralisation goals in Monze and beyond.
